assessment.reason: Low-volume recent usage cleared 1.5 in half of the logged games. That record makes +170 plausible versus the break-even, with the best price among six books. The edge rests on the model beating a tight market consensus.
assessment.model_case: Mims averaged two to three targets with a solid catch rate and logged two catches in four of eight games. The projection of about 1.8 catches comes mostly from base usage. Defense and venue adjustments are small, so no single adjustment is doing excessive work.
assessment.price_case: Every book's main line is 1.5. BetRivers at +170 beats the +145 to +158 range elsewhere. Break-even roughly matches the no-vig consensus, so the value depends entirely on the model rather than on market mispricing.
assessment.context_case: No Mims-specific reporting was supplied, so his status is unverified. Weeks 2, 3 and 10 are absent from the sample, and the reason is unknown.

qualitative_review.countercase: With a two-target role, one fewer look sinks the Over. A Denver lead against a Rudolph-led offense could tilt the game toward the run. Poor weather could also cut passing volume. Raw-to-calibrated shrinkage still leaves a large model-market gap that five books dispute.

findings.note: In this Nov 26 CBS article, SportsLine's model picks Over 36.5, projects 40 combined points and has the Over hitting in 57% of simulations. It notes the Over has hit in each of Denver's last four games. Pittsburgh is starting Mason Rudolph after releasing Aaron Rodgers.

Covers' Nov 26 page forecasts about 17 mph southwest winds with gusts near 28 mph, around 42F, and a 65% chance of rain at kickoff. It lists Pittsburgh LBs Highsmith (ankle) and Herbig (hip/ribs) as iffy, and Neil Parker picks Broncos -4.5 rather than a total.

Neil Parker's early Covers pick from Nov 23 was Under 38.5, citing Pittsburgh's one-dimensional offense and the Steelers allowing 18 points per home game. The line has since dropped, from a 40.5 open to 36.5 at other books, so Bovada's 37 now gives only half a point more than the market.

ESPN's game log shows Mims with 1-2 catches in each of his last five games, including just 1 in each of the last two, with 11 catches on 18 targets in 2026; its blurb calls him an unappealing fantasy option for Friday's Steelers game.
A preview from one day ago says Sean Payton keeps calling it a priority to find new ways to get Mims the ball, but against the Raiders he had only three offensive touches and some snaps at fullback.
Preseason context: Courtland Sutton and the newly added Jaylen Waddle lead Denver's receivers, which limits targets for Mims as a depth receiver who also returns kicks and punts.

With Nolan Traore out 8-10 weeks with a hamstring injury, Brown started Monday at Minnesota with his minutes restriction lifted and had 17 points and a career-high 7 assists in 29 minutes.
The NBA.com fantasy rookie rankings expect Brown to handle the ball more as long as Brooklyn keeps starting him, and say the Nets drafted him for his playmaking.
Brown averages 3.8 APG. His last five games had 7, 0, 4, 5 and 2 assists, with 3 of 5 over 3.5, though the lower games came off the bench on limited minutes (18-27 min).
